body:
Found by Fable review probes at the s461 round-18 merge (extending #931 repro pairs); PRE-EXISTING on main 72930b7 AND on the #931 tree -- NOT a #931 regression (probed both).

REPRO (3 lines):
  sub ok { print(($_[0] ? "ok" : "not ok"), " - $_[1]\n") }
  $_ = "zzz";
  ok /q*/, "four";
perl prints "ok - four" (empty q* pattern matches).  PCL dies at LOAD:
"Comma not inside a backquote" -- and only by the ACCIDENT of the comma.

MECHANISM: PPI lexes the pattern text as the q* QUOTE OPERATOR -- `q*/, "four";...*` is a Quote::Literal running to the next `*` (or EOF), so the statement tokenizes as `ok / <q-string>`.  _repair_word_match (#931, now fixpoint) DECLINES: its closing-/ scan finds no second `/` token (it is inside the quote token).  The mis-parse stands as a DIVISION, and the emitted CL is
  (p-/ (p-scalar-ctx (pl-ok))
    q*/, "four";
  )
-- the quote token content emitted VERBATIM as raw Perl text.  TWO bugs:
(1) the repair family cannot see a swallowed closing `/` inside a
    manufactured quote token (same family as #931 sub-case; the sibling
    letters x/y/m/s/tr adjacent to `/` likely do the same -- `ok /x*/`,
    `ok /m*/` etc. -- PROBE the family before fixing);
(2) LOUDNESS IS AN ACCIDENT: whatever the parse does, raw Perl text must
    never reach the emission -- with different content the CL could READ
    and run garbage silently (#138 family, worse than a drop).  The
    emitter/seam that printed the token verbatim should refuse/drop LOUDLY.
Do not fix in the $end_pars region (docs/pexpr-term-parsing-review.md); the repair layer (_repair_word_match_pass widening: treat a Quote token whose DELIMITER region contains `/` after a WORD-/ site as part of the derail and re-lex the text) is the likely layer, per the #931/#563 precedent.

=== SHIPPED s462at (agent AT, round 19), BOTH halves, and half (ii) turned out
=== to be a one-line seam that had nothing to do with the parse.

HALF (ii), THE LOUDNESS -- fixed first, because it is what makes half (i) safe
to get wrong.  `Pl::ExprToCL::convert_perl_string_form` ends in
`else { # Unknown format, return as-is; return $str }` -- the token's RAW PERL
TEXT, emitted straight into the CL.  It now returns
`['p-unparsable-quote', <the token, truncated to 60 chars>]`: a form that READS
and dies where the value would have been used, naming the token.  That is
`p-unrepresentable-char`'s shape (#419), the same `%p-unsupported-value` helper,
and it is trappable by `eval { }`.  `docs/not-supported.md` entry added.

HALF (i), THE PARSE -- `_match_close_after` also answers yes when the token
IMMEDIATELY after the mis-lexed `/` is a quote-like token spelled with an
OPERATOR letter and a non-word delimiter and containing a `/`
(`_manufactured_quote_close`).

THE FAMILY, PROBED BEFORE FIXING, as the task asked (5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
every quote-like letter derails and the CLASS of the manufactured token
follows the letter -- q/qq give a Quote::Literal/Quote::Interpolate, m/s/y/tr
give a Regexp::Match/Substitute/Transliterate, and `x` does not derail at all
because `x` is not a quote-like letter.  12 rows: 4 SAME before, 9 after.

THE BREAKING CASE, AND IT IS REAL -- caught by the 1029-file emission A/B, not
by probes.  The first version scanned the WHOLE statement for a quote-like
token containing `/`.  `t/re/pat.t:113` is
`ok /bcd|xyz/, qq [\$_ = '$_'; /bcd|xyz/];` -- the DESCRIPTION contains `/`, and
the token before the real closing delimiter is the Word `xyz`, so the loose test
"found a close" there too and repaired the closing `/` as well: the pattern came
out `m/bcd|xyzmmmm/`, one `m` per fixpoint round.  Hence STRICTLY the next
token.  That shape is now an inverse row in the guard (it passes on the base
tree).

AND THE OTHER DIRECTION, also probed rather than assumed: PERL'S OWN LEXER
licenses the repair wherever it fires.  `sub w {8} print w / 2, " a/b\n";` is a
SYNTAX ERROR in perl ("Unknown regexp modifier \"/b\""), i.e. perl reads that
`/` as a match too; four such rows (declared sub + `q{}`/`qq{}`/a plain string
after a division) confirm it, and they stay DIVISIONS in PCL only because
`_word_is_term` takes a declared sub out before the scan runs.

RESIDUE, filed as #962 and NOT a #940 bug: three rows (`q+`, `qq*`, `tr*`)
still disagree, and the parse is now right in all three.  A FAILED capture-LESS
m// returns a false ELEMENT in list context where perl returns `()`, so
`ok /pat/, "desc"` on a miss hands the sub ("", "desc") instead of ("desc") and
every argument shifts.

BARS MET.  corpus-diff over 111: IDENTICAL for this change (the one file that
moves is #939's).  Emission A/B over 1029 files (perl-tests + lib + cpan
modules + perl's own t/): SAME=1027 DIFF=2 RCDIFF=0, and the 2 are #939's.
Gate-SET scan over BOTH populations, 638 files, vs a 4c354bc worktree:
IDENTICAL -- no file's compiler verdict moved, which is the bar for a widened
decline.  Full sweep GATE clean, TOTAL 18342 -> 18343 (#939's row), drops 5 =
census.  Guard `Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t` 66 -> 71: one test_transpile with the
five derailing letters, the `x` control, a real `q*â¦*` after a real division,
a real `q*â¦*` string, and the pat.t:113 shape; plus four rows for half (ii)
asserting BOTH that the death form is emitted and that the raw token text is
not.  Inverse-verified on the 4c354bc worktree: rows 68-71 fail there.
PPI report: `docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md` Â§11c (with the per-letter table) and
`docs/ppi-bug-report.t` Bug 8c (2 rows, 56 -> 58), both failing on PPI 1.291
as a bug-report row must.
description: s463f (Fable merge review, 2026-09-01): MERGED to main as 6e6f191 (AT worktree rebased over 12eacb5; the two conflicts were the DECIDED/session-log tops, both sections kept).  Fable probes vs perl 5.40.3: #939 19-row file SAME (substr/vec/pos/$#a targets, hash/array element bases, list/scalar/boolean contexts, tr, !~, /g, for-alias, m// unmoved); #934 25-row file SAME except the E-class row (fallback=>1 with nothing to autogenerate: PCL small vs perl big) = #961, pre-existing and filed by AT; #940 11-row file SAME once the probe rows that are INVALID PERL were dropped (a declared sub followed by `/ 3, "\n"` is a perl syntax error too).  Status flipped from open.
title: WORD / derail meets the q* QUOTE OPERATOR: `ok /q*/, "four";` emits RAW PERL TEXT into the CL
